files.Title: Egami.Alignment

files.Title: Egami.Analysis.ChannelDifference
files.Summary: How much one channel of two images differs, on the 0 to 1 scale of the channel values, so 8-bit and 16-bit results line up.

files.Title: Egami.Analysis.ChannelStatistics
files.Summary: The statistics of one channel over a frame, on the 0 to 1 scale of the channel values, as ImageMagick's identify -verbose reports them.

files.Title: Egami.Analysis.CompareOptions

files.Title: Egami.Analysis.CompareResult
files.Summary: What found: each channel's difference, the overall one, and how many pixels differ.

files.Title: Egami.Analysis.DominantColorOptions
files.Summary: Options for .

files.Title: Egami.Analysis.Histogram
files.Summary: How many pixels of a frame have each value of one channel, in equal bins over 0 to 1, from .

files.Title: Egami.Analysis.PerceptualHash
files.Summary: 64-bit perceptual hashes: images that look alike get hashes a few bits apart, however they were compressed or resized, so the between two hashes says how alike two pictures are. Store the hashes as keys to find near-duplicates.

files.Title: Egami.Analysis.RasterStatistics
files.Summary: The statistics of each channel of a frame, from .

files.Title: Egami.Analysis.WeightedColor
files.Summary: A color and the share of an image's pixels it stands for, from .

files.Title: Egami.Axis
files.Summary: The direction images are laid out in by .

files.Title: Egami.ChromaDownsampling
files.Summary: How chroma is reduced to the chroma resolution when a raster converts to a subsampled .

files.Title: Egami.ChromaUpsampling
files.Summary: How chroma is brought up to luma resolution when a converts to RGB.

files.Title: Egami.ClearMode
files.Summary: Says whether new pixel memory is cleared.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.Chromaticity
files.Summary: A CIE 1931 chromaticity: the x and y coordinates of a color with its brightness left out.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.CmykColor
files.Summary: A CMYK color: ink amounts 0 to 1, 0 being no ink, by the plain formula (K = 1 − max(R, G, B), C = (1 − R − K) / (1 − K)) on encoded sRGB. Real inks need a print profile: converts through one.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.ColorCodePoints
files.Summary: The ITU-T H.273 code points that PNG's cICP chunk, AVIF and JPEG XL use to name a color encoding: colour primaries, transfer characteristics, matrix coefficients and the full-range flag, kept exactly as stored so codes Egami does not know round-trip.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.ColorConvert
files.Summary: Converts between color values (), through XYZ D65, and between rows of pixels and color values.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.ColorModel
files.Summary: Whether a color encoding has three RGB channels, one gray channel, four CMYK inks, or the inks of an n-colour press.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.ColorPrimaries
files.Summary: The chromaticities of an RGB color space's red, green and blue primaries and of its white. With a transfer function they make a .

files.Title: Egami.Colors.ColorProfile
files.Summary: What a raster's numbers mean: the color model, the primaries and white point, and the transfer function. Immutable; the built-ins cover the common encodings, and makes any other RGB encoding.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.ColorTransform
files.Summary: A conversion from one color encoding to another, compiled once and then applied to spans of pixels of any type. Reusable and safe to share between threads. Transforms are cached per , so creating the same one again is cheap.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.ColorTransformOptions
files.Summary: How a color conversion maps colors: the rendering intent, black point compensation, and for HDR sources, tone mapping, the source peak and reference white.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.Colorant
files.Summary: A named ink: a process ink, a spot colour or a technical ink, with how it looks for backends that cannot print it. Names are matched exactly (ordinal, case-sensitive), as PDF matches them; the names Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Black always mean the process inks, as in PDF's DeviceN. Two colorants are equal when their names are.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.ColorantKind
files.Summary: What a colorant is for, as PDF and ICC name inks.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.GainMap
files.Summary: An HDR gain map: a small image that, with , turns an SDR base image into its HDR rendition (or the reverse). Read from Ultra HDR, ISO 21496-1 and Apple JPEG files into ; written back by the JPEG writer. Immutable, so rasters can share it.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.GainMapFormat
files.Summary: Where a gain map's metadata came from.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.GainMapInfo
files.Summary: How a gain map turns its base image into another rendition, in ISO 21496-1's terms: for a gain map sample g (0 to 1) after gamma, the log2 boost is lerp(, , g), applied as (base + ) × 2^(boost × weight) − , where the weight rises from 0 at a display headroom of to 1 at . Boosts and capacities are log2 values.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.GainMapOptions
files.Summary: How and make a gain map (HDR Design question 10). The defaults are libultrahdr's: a full-size map with a gain for each of red, green and blue, gamma 1, encoded at quality 95.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.GainMapValues
files.Summary: A value for each of red, green and blue; a one-channel gain map has the same three.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.HdrMetadata
files.Summary: What an HDR file says about the display it was mastered on and the light levels in it (SMPTE ST 2086 and CTA-861.3, as PNG's mDCV and cLLI chunks store them). Tone mapping takes its source peak from here. Luminances are in cd/m².

files.Title: Egami.Colors.HslColor
files.Summary: An HSL color: hue, saturation and lightness of encoded sRGB, as CSS hsl() defines them.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.HsvColor
files.Summary: An HSV (HSB) color: hue, saturation and value of encoded sRGB, as color pickers use them.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.IColorValue<TSelf>
files.Summary: A color value in one color model, convertible to and from CIE XYZ (D65) and sRGB pixels, so can convert between any two models and between pixels and values.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.IccData
files.Summary: A parsed ICC profile (ICC.1, versions 2 and 4): the header fields, the description and copyright text, and every tag with its bytes. Read-only; turns it into an encoding that conversion can use.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.IccProfileClass
files.Summary: What an ICC profile describes, from its header's class field.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.IccTag
files.Summary: One tag of an ICC profile: its signature, the type signature its data starts with, and the data.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.InkAppearance
files.Summary: How an ink looks at full tint where it cannot be printed: on an RGB canvas, in SVG, in a proof of a raster without its plate, or drawn into the process inks of a raster that lacks it. A process CMYK colour, an sRGB colour or a Lab colour, as PDF's alternate colour spaces allow.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.InkAppearanceKind
files.Summary: The colour model an is given in.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.InkColor
files.Summary: A colour given as inks: named colorants with tints, as PDF's Separation and DeviceN colours, plus the appearance other backends draw. An ink canvas paints each named ink's plate; an RGB canvas, SVG or a raster without the ink draws . Immutable.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.InkSet
files.Summary: The inks a printed page uses, fixed when an ink raster is made: the process inks of an output profile, then named spot and technical inks, at most in all. Colours naming an ink the set lacks are drawn through their appearance into the process inks, as PDF does for a device without that colorant. Immutable: and return a new set.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.InkTint
files.Summary: One ink of an and its tint.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.LabColor
files.Summary: A CIE Lab* color relative to D50, as ICC and CSS Color 4 define Lab.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.LchColor
files.Summary: A CIE LCh color: the polar form of (D50), with chroma and hue instead of a and b.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.OklabColor
files.Summary: An Oklab color (Björn Ottosson, 2020): a perceptual space built on linear sRGB, where equal distances look about equally different and hues stay put when lightness or chroma changes. CSS Color 4's oklab().

files.Title: Egami.Colors.OklchColor
files.Summary: An Oklch color: the polar form of , CSS Color 4's oklch().

files.Title: Egami.Colors.RenderingIntent
files.Summary: How a color conversion handles colors the target cannot show, with the ICC numbering (0 to 3).

files.Title: Egami.Colors.ToneMapping
files.Summary: How HDR light above reference white is brought into the 0..1 range of an SDR encoding.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.TransferFunction
files.Summary: How a color space encodes light: the curve from stored values to linear light and back. Single values use exact double arithmetic; rows of floats use a vectorized form within 1e-5 of it (PQ rows use the double form), the same on every CPU with or without SIMD.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.XyzColor
files.Summary: A CIE 1931 XYZ color relative to D65 white (Y = 1 for white), CSS Color 4's XYZ; adapts it.

files.Title: Egami.Colors.YCbCrColor
files.Summary: A Y'CbCr color: luma and two chroma differences of encoded sRGB, scaled as 8-bit codes / 255: at full range chroma is centered on 128 / 255, as JPEG and H.273 store it, so a byte reads as value × 255. The members without options use BT.601 at full range, as JPEG does; overloads take a and , from the coefficient table planar YUV images share.

files.Title: Egami.CorruptDataException
files.Summary: Thrown when data matches a format but breaks its rules, such as a bad checksum, a truncated stream or an invalid table.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssAngle
files.Summary: An angle, converted to degrees from deg, grad, rad or turn.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssAttribute
files.Summary: An attribute of an element, as lists it.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssCalc
files.Summary: A length, percentage or number that may be a math function: calc() with + - * / and parentheses, and min(), max() and clamp() (CSS Values 4), nested freely. A plain length or number parses too, so a consumer can handle every <length-percentage> the same way. turns it into pixels once the consumer knows what each unit is worth.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssCascade
files.Summary: The cascade (CSS Cascade 5, without animations, transitions and cascade layers): finds the declarations that apply to an element (or, for rules, a page) and picks the winner for each property.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssCascadeOptions
files.Summary: Options for building a .

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssCascadedStyle
files.Summary: The cascaded style of an element: the winning declaration of each property, with its origin.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssColor
files.Summary: A CSS color (CSS Color 4) converted to sRGB: red, green, blue and alpha from 0 to 1, gamma-encoded, clipped to the sRGB gamut; or currentcolor.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssComponentValue
files.Summary: A CSS Syntax 3 component value: a preserved token, a function or a simple block. Declarations, preludes and values are lists of these. serializes back to CSS text.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssComputedStyle
files.Summary: An element's computed style, as far as CSS defines it generically: CSS-wide keywords resolved, inheritance applied, custom properties and var() substituted. Values stay component values; the consumer parses each property by its type (and resolves relative units, percentages and currentcolor).

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssDeclaration
files.Summary: A CSS declaration: a property name, its value as component values, and whether it is !important.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssFont
files.Summary: The font shorthand (CSS Fonts 4), parsed.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssFontFace
files.Summary: The descriptors of an rule (CSS Fonts 4), parsed. Invalid descriptors keep their defaults.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssFontFaceRule
files.Summary: An rule.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssFontFamily
files.Summary: One entry of a font family list: a family name or a generic family keyword.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssFontFamilyList
files.Summary: A font-family value: family names (quoted, or unquoted identifier sequences) and generic families.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssFontSource
files.Summary: One source of an src descriptor: a URL with its format and technologies, or a local font.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssFontWeight
files.Summary: A font-weight value.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssFontWeightKind
files.Summary: How a was given.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssFunction
files.Summary: A function: its name and its arguments up to the closing parenthesis.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssImportRule
files.Summary: An rule. Egami.Css does not fetch it: the consumer may load the sheet and pass it to the cascade.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssLayerRule
files.Summary: An rule: a statement naming layers, or a block of rules. Cascade layers are not implemented: the cascade treats the rules inside a layer block as ordinary rules in their place.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssLength
files.Summary: A length (or percentage, or unitless number) with its unit, such as 12px or 50%.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssMarginBox
files.Summary: The sixteen page-margin boxes around a page's content (CSS Paged Media 3 section 5.1), clockwise from the top left.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssMatrixTransform
files.Summary: matrix(a, b, c, d, e, f).

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssMediaContext
files.Summary: The environment media queries are evaluated against: the media type, the viewport and the user's preferences.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssMediaQueryList
files.Summary: A media query list (Media Queries 4), such as screen and (min-width: 600px), print.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssMediaRule
files.Summary: An rule: rules that apply when the media query list matches.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssNamespaceRule
files.Summary: An rule: a prefix (or the default namespace) for selectors.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssNamespaces
files.Summary: The namespace prefixes selectors may use (svg|rect, [xlink|href]) and the default namespace for type selectors, as rules declare them. Prefixes are case-sensitive.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssOrigin
files.Summary: The origin of a style sheet in the cascade.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssPage
files.Summary: A page being laid out, as page selectors see it: its page type (the page property of the content that starts it) and whether it is the first, a left or a blank page.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssPageMarginRule
files.Summary: A page-margin rule inside , such as { content: counter(page) }.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssPageOrientation
files.Summary: Whether a page size asks for portrait or landscape pages.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssPagePseudoClasses
files.Summary: The page pseudo-classes a page selector tests (CSS Paged Media 3 section 4.3).

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssPageRule
files.Summary: An rule (CSS Paged Media 3): page selectors, the declarations for the page context (size, margin, padding, border, background, inherited text properties) and its page-margin rules.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssPageSelector
files.Summary: One selector of an rule, such as chapter:first.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssPageSize
files.Summary: The size descriptor of (CSS Paged Media 3 section 7.1): auto, one or two lengths, or a page size name such as A4 or letter with an optional orientation.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssPageStyle
files.Summary: The cascaded style of one page: the page context's winning declarations and those of each page-margin box any rule styles. Compute the page context with the root element's computed style as its parent, and each margin box with the page context's computed style as its parent.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssParseError
files.Summary: A problem found while parsing CSS. Parsing recovers as CSS Syntax 3 says and goes on.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssParseOptions
files.Summary: Options for parsing CSS.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssPropertyDefinition
files.Summary: A longhand property the cascade knows: whether it inherits, its initial value, and optionally how to validate a value.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssPropertyRegistry
files.Summary: The properties the cascade knows. gives the common text properties of CSS; consumers add their own, such as Egami.Svg's fill and stroke. Unregistered properties cascade too, as non-inherited properties without an initial value. Do not change a registry while a cascade built from it is in use.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssRange
files.Summary: A range of numbers, such as a weight range 100 900; a single value has equal ends.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssRotateTransform
files.Summary: rotate(angle), or SVG's rotate(angle cx cy) about a center.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssRule
files.Summary: A rule of a style sheet.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssScaleTransform
files.Summary: scale(), scaleX() or scaleY() (percentages are converted to factors).

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssSelector
files.Summary: One complex selector of a selector list, such as svg|g > rect.highlight:first-child.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssSelectorList
files.Summary: A selector list (Selectors 4), such as a style rule's prelude or the argument of querySelectorAll.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssShorthandDefinition
files.Summary: A shorthand property: its longhands and how to expand a value into them.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssSimpleBlock
files.Summary: A simple block: content between matching (), [] or {}.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssSkewTransform
files.Summary: skew(), skewX() or skewY().

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssSpecificity
files.Summary: A selector's specificity (Selectors 4): IDs, then classes, attributes and pseudo-classes, then types and pseudo-elements.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssStyleRule
files.Summary: A style rule: a selector list and declarations, such as rect.a { fill: red }.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssStyleSheet
files.Summary: A parsed CSS style sheet (CSS Syntax 3 "parse a stylesheet", with the rules CSS defines interpreted).

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssSupportsRule
files.Summary: An rule: rules that apply when the condition holds.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssToken
files.Summary: One CSS token, with its position in the source.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssTokenKind
files.Summary: The kinds of token the CSS Syntax 3 tokenizer produces.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssTokenValue
files.Summary: A token kept as a component value: any token other than a function or an opening bracket.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssTokenizer
files.Summary: The CSS Syntax 3 tokenizer (section 4), with its input preprocessing.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssTransformFunction
files.Summary: One transform function of a .

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssTransformList
files.Summary: A CSS transform value (CSS Transforms 1), or SVG's transform attribute: a list of transform functions applied left to right, as nested coordinate systems.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssTransformOrigin
files.Summary: A transform-origin value.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssTranslateTransform
files.Summary: translate(), translateX() or translateY().

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssUnicodeRange
files.Summary: A range of code points from unicode-range, such as U+0000-00FF.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssUnit
files.Summary: CSS length units (CSS Values 4), plus for a unitless number and .

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssUnknownAtRule
files.Summary: An at-rule Egami.Css does not interpret, such as or , kept as component values.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssUnsupportedTransform
files.Summary: A 3D transform function (such as rotateX() or matrix3d()) that parsed but a 2D renderer cannot apply.

files.Title: Egami.Css.CssUrl
files.Summary: A URL from url(...) (quoted or not) or src(...).

files.Title: Egami.Css.ICssElement
files.Summary: An element that selectors match against: implemented by a document tree such as Egami.Svg's or an HTML DOM.

files.Title: Egami.DecodeStatus
files.Summary: Where a stands, as reports it.

files.Title: Egami.DiagnosticLevel
files.Summary: How much an matters. Maps one to one onto the Debug, Information and Warning log levels.

files.Title: Egami.DiagnosticReporter
files.Summary: One call's link to , with the same level filter and per-id cap Egami's own readers and writers use. Get one from at the start of a call (format plug-ins use ) and dispose it when the call ends. When the context has no handler it is a shared instance that does nothing, so reporting costs one check.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Annotation
files.Summary: A link or a destination for : what a document backend writes, and pixels never show.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.AnnotationKind
files.Summary: What an marks, as Skia's annotations do.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.BlendPaint
files.Summary: Two paints combined pixel by pixel with a blend mode, as Skia's blend shader: is blended onto , and the result is what this paint draws. Each part keeps its own and (its blend mode, blur and dithering are not used), inside this paint's own local matrix.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.BlurStyle
files.Summary: How a keeps or removes the blurred shape's inside and outside, as Skia's blur styles.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Canvas
files.Summary:
A surface to draw paths, shapes, strokes and images on, through a current transform and clip. The canvas itself is abstract: draws into pixels, and other backends (a PDF page, a recorder) keep the calls as vectors. Every public call is checked and tracked here (the transform, the clip bounds, the save stack) and then ends in exactly one protected On hook, which is all a backend overrides; hooks added in later versions get default bodies, so adding them never breaks a backend.

Coordinates are float pixels, y down; the pixel at (0, 0) covers the square from 0 to 1. Calls draw when they are made. A canvas is for one thread at a time; one large call may still spread its rows over several cores.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.CanvasOptions
files.Summary: Settings for a raster canvas.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.ClipOp
files.Summary: Whether a clip keeps what is inside a shape or what is outside it.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.ColorMatrixPaint
files.Summary: Another paint with a color matrix run on its colors, as Skia's color-filtered shader: each color, unpremultiplied, goes through the matrix, is clamped to 0 to 1 and is premultiplied again. makes one.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.ConicalGradient
files.Summary: A gradient between two circles, as the HTML canvas's createRadialGradient, Skia's two-point conical gradient and a PDF type 3 shading define it: for each t, the circle whose center and radius are t of the way from the start circle to the end one; a pixel takes the largest t whose circle passes through it with a radius of at least 0. It covers a focal point inside a circle (a start radius of 0), one circle inside the other, and cones drawn on one side only.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.ContourMeasure
files.Summary: One measured contour of a . Distances run from 0 at the contour's start to at its end; distances outside are clamped to them, as in Skia.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.CornerRadii
files.Summary: The x and y radius of each corner of a , clockwise from the top-left. A radius below 0 counts as 0, and a corner with either radius 0 is square.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.CustomPaint
files.Summary: A paint whose colors come from C# code: override to fill a row of premultiplied float colors. Rows are shaded in parallel bands, so must be thread-safe and must give a pixel the same color whichever band or thread asks; then the result is the same at any core count. A backend that keeps vectors, such as a PDF page, cannot run C# and draws the call through its raster fallback instead. Derive a record class from it.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.DashPattern
files.Summary: The dashes of a stroke: lengths of drawn and skipped stretches in turn, in path units, and where in the pattern each contour starts, as PDF's d, SVG's stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset, and Skia's dash effect define them. An odd number of lengths repeats once to make an even one, as SVG says, and a pattern whose lengths add up to 0 draws a solid line. Each dash is an open piece of the path that follows its curves and gets the stroke's caps; the pattern starts afresh on each contour.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.DrawingExtensions
files.Summary: Ways into a canvas from Egami's rasters and operation chains.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.EncodedImage
files.Summary: An image kept as its file's bytes, such as a JPEG, for : a backend that can store the bytes as they are, as a PDF page stores a JPEG as DCTDecode, gets them through OnDrawEncodedImage without decoding and encoding again; every other backend draws the decoded pixels. The bytes are probed when the image is made and decoded at most once, on first need. Immutable and thread-safe.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.FallbackImage
files.Summary: A drawing call rendered into pixels by Canvas.RasterizeFallback, for a backend to place as an image.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.FillRule
files.Summary: Which points a filled path covers, from how often its outline winds around them.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.FontExtensions
files.Summary: Glyphs and text as s in canvas units, y down, for clipping, stroking or measuring them as shapes.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.GlyphCache
files.Summary: The process-wide cache of glyph coverage masks the raster canvas draws small text from: one mask per typeface (each variation position its own), glyph, device em size, axis scales, subpixel phase, edging, hinting and synthesis, for glyphs up to 256 device pixels per em under a scale-and-translate transform. Masks hold one byte per pixel, or three for LCD edging. Bigger, rotated or skewed glyphs fill as paths and are not cached. Masks are rendered by the same rasterizer as paths and drawn at the same rounded positions either way, so the cache changes speed, never pixels. Shared by every canvas on every thread; least recently used masks go first when the budget is spent.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Gradient
files.Summary: A paint whose color changes along a line, around a center or between two circles by its stops. Each pixel center maps back through the canvas transform and to a position t along the gradient, which brings into 0 to 1 and the stops turn into a color. On 8-bit targets t picks one of 1024 colors made once per paint; float and 16-bit targets mix the stops exactly.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.GradientInterpolation
files.Summary: How a gradient mixes its stops: the color space, as CSS Color 4 defines them, and for the way around the hue circle.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.GradientStop
files.Summary: One color of a gradient at a position along it, from 0 (the start) to 1 (the end). Two stops at the same offset make a hard edge: the later one applies from that offset on. A gradient whose first stop is after 0 or whose last is before 1 repeats the nearest stop's color to the end, as CSS does.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.HueMethod
files.Summary: Which way around the hue circle an Oklch gradient goes between two stops, as CSS Color 4's hue interpolation methods.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.IColorGlyphRenderer
files.Summary: Draws color glyphs of a format Egami.Drawing does not draw itself, such as the SVG documents of an OpenType SVG table (Egami.Svg's SvgGlyphRenderer). Set on , it is asked first for every glyph whose font has that format, except where the font has a COLR version 1 glyph, so the order is COLR v1, the renderer, COLR v0, sbix, CBDT, then the outline.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.ImagePaint
files.Summary: An image as a paint: shapes are filled with the image's pixels, pixel (0, 0) covering the paint-space square from 0 to 1, under and the canvas transform. and say what lies past its edges, so it tiles as a pattern, and leaves the outside transparent, as image masks and stencils need. When the paint shrinks the image, sampling reads the nearest smaller level of a .

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.InkCanvas
files.Summary: A canvas that draws into an 's plates: printing inks instead of RGB. It shares 's rasterizer, clips and layers, so shapes, strokes and text cover exactly the same pixels; where the RGB canvas blends colours, this one sets each plate. A paint's prints its inks by name (inks the raster lacks through their appearance into the process inks); RGB colours, gradients and images convert into the process inks through and the ink set's profile.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.InkCanvasOptions
files.Summary: How an turns colours that are not inks into its process inks.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.InterpolationSpace
files.Summary: The color space a gradient's stops are mixed in.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Lattice
files.Summary: A grid over an image for , as Skia's lattice: the x and y divisions cut the image into columns and rows that alternate fixed and stretchable, starting with fixed, so a division at the image's left or top edge makes the first column or row stretchable. Fixed columns and rows keep their size when the destination is large enough and shrink in proportion when it is not; stretchable ones share what is left. A nine-patch is the lattice with two divisions each way.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.LatticeCellKind
files.Summary: What a cell of a draws.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.LayerOptions
files.Summary: How a layer started by is merged at the matching : filtered, masked, faded by and blended into what lies below with , through the clip. A layer is what PDF calls a transparency group.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.LineCap
files.Summary: How the ends of an open stroked contour look.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.LineJoin
files.Summary: How a stroke turns the corner where two segments meet.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.LinearGradient
files.Summary: A gradient along a line: t is 0 on the line through square to it, and 1 through .

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.MarkedContent
files.Summary: A tag that brackets a run of drawing for a document backend, as PDF's marked content (BMC, BDC and EMC): a structure element of tagged PDF (a paragraph, a heading, a figure), an artifact such as a page number, or a span with replacement text.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.MaskBlur
files.Summary: A Gaussian blur of a shape's coverage before the paint is applied, as Skia's blur mask filter: is in device pixels, so it does not scale with the canvas transform. Set it as . Egami blurs with its fast blur; an axis-aligned rectangle with is computed exactly from the error function, which is faster still.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Mesh
files.Summary: Triangles with an optional color, texture coordinate or value at each vertex, for : Gouraud-shaded triangles, textured triangles (a paint mapped through the texture coordinates) and PDF's free-form and lattice-form shadings (one value per vertex, mapped through gradient stops). Immutable: the constructor copies what it is given.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.MeshMode
files.Summary: How a reads its vertices (or its indices, when it has them) as triangles.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.NinePatch
files.Summary: An image with its , as Android's nine-patch (.9.png) files hold them.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.NoisePaint
files.Summary: Procedural noise as a paint. and follow SVG 1.1's feTurbulence step by step (its random table, lattice and gradients), so the pixels match Skia's noise shaders and browsers within rounding; is smoother and can tile. Each of the four channels is its own noise, straight alpha included. The noise lives in paint coordinates: it scales and turns with the canvas transform and .

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.NoisePaintKind
files.Summary: The kind of noise a makes.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Overprint
files.Summary: Which plates a paint prints on an ink canvas, as PDF's overprint; see .

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Paint
files.Summary:
What a drawing call puts on the canvas, and how it combines with what is there: the colors (from the subclass), the , an , whether edges are antialiased, and for shapes an optional . The kinds are , the gradients (, , , ), , , , and . A color converts to a solid paint where a paint is expected. A paint is an , so a paragraph's text style can carry it.

A paint other than a solid one has its own coordinates: maps them into the canvas's local coordinates, so a gradient or an image turns and scales with the canvas transform, and further with its own matrix.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Patch
files.Summary:
A curved four-sided surface with a color, value or texture coordinate at each corner, for : PDF's Coons and tensor-product patch shadings (types 6 and 7) and Skia's drawPatch. The surface's parameters u (left to right) and v (top to bottom) run from 0 to 1; corner data is interpolated bilinearly in them. Immutable.

Corners are in the order top-left (u 0, v 0), top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. A Coons patch's 12 points go clockwise from the top-left corner, as Skia's: the top curve left to right (points 0 to 3), the right curve down (3 to 6), the bottom curve right to left (6 to 9) and the left curve up (9, 10, 11, 0). A tensor patch's 16 points are its net row by row, top row first, each row left to right.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PatchKind
files.Summary: Which surface a is: its boundary only, or a full tensor-product net.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Path
files.Summary: An outline of contours made of lines, quadratic and cubic Bézier curves, with the that says which points it covers when filled. A path never changes after it is built, so one path can be drawn from many threads and kept by any canvas backend. Coordinates are float pixels, y down. Build one with or a shape helper such as .

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PathBuilder
files.Summary: Builds a one command at a time. Arcs, ovals and round corners become cubic curves as they are added, so a path holds only lines, quadratics and cubics. A line or curve with no contour open starts one at the last contour's start (or the origin), as SVG and Skia do. Building takes time in proportion to the points added; copies them, so the builder can go on or be reused.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PathDirection
files.Summary: The direction a shape's outline runs, on a y-down screen.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PathEffect
files.Summary: Turns one path into another before it is filled or stroked: dashes, rounded corners, trimming, jitter, shapes stamped along the path, hatching. Effects are immutable, so one can be shared and reused; and combine them. Apply one with , or set it on to have the canvas apply it before stroking. The set is Skia's: dash, corner, trim, discrete, 1D path, 2D line and 2D path effects, composed and summed.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PathMeasure
files.Summary: Measures a path: the length of each contour, and the point, direction and pieces at any distance along it. Lengths are exact to about 1e-4 units, curves included: each curve's length is integrated by adaptive Gauss–Legendre quadrature, and a distance is turned back into a point on the curve by Newton steps, so long curves do not gather the errors of a flattened outline. Contours of zero length are left out, as Skia's SkContourMeasureIter leaves them. Measuring is done once, here; the queries are cheap and safe from many threads.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PathOp
files.Summary: How and combine the areas of two paths: Skia's five operations.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PathVerb
files.Summary: One drawing command of a ; the comment on each says how many points it takes.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Picture
files.Summary: Recorded canvas calls, from a or : replay them on any canvas with or , fill shapes with them through a , render them with , or keep them in an .egdr file with . Replay is always vector, so a picture stays sharp at any scale. Immutable, and safe to replay on several threads and canvases at once.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PicturePaint
files.Summary: A as a paint: a tiling pattern, the shape of PDF's and SVG's tiling patterns and Skia's picture shader. The rectangle of the picture, in its own coordinates, is repeated by and under and the canvas transform. The raster backend renders one tile at the device scale the paint is drawn at and keeps it with the picture, so a pattern stays sharp when zoomed and is rendered once for repeated fills at one scale. A tile is at most 4096 pixels a side.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PictureRecorder
files.Summary: A canvas that records instead of picture: every hook call is kept with its arguments, and returns them as an immutable to replay on any canvas, at any scale, as often as needed, as Skia's SkPictureRecorder. Any code that draws on a can draw into it. Paths, paints, images and nested pictures are kept by reference: images must not change while the picture is in use.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PixelGeometry
files.Summary: The order of a display's color subpixels, which LCD text edging needs to know.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PlaceholderPainter
files.Summary: Draws a placeholder's content where left room for it.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.PointMode
files.Summary: How reads its points.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.RadialGradient
files.Summary: A gradient in circles around a center: t is the distance from divided by .

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.RasterCanvas<TPixel>
files.Summary:
The raster backend: a canvas that draws into a raster's pixels, with exact-area antialiasing, blended through Egami's Compositor in the pixel type's own precision. A clip that is a pixel-aligned rectangle stays a rectangle; any other clip becomes a coverage mask over the clip's bounds. A call whose area exceeds 256 KiB of destination rows spreads its rows over up to cores, with the same pixels at any core count.

A layer from is premultiplied in the raster's class (PremulRgba8 for 8-bit rasters, PremulRgbaF32 for deeper ones) and covers only its bounds inside the clip, grown by its filter's reach; its memory comes from the raster's and is released at .

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.RectF
files.Summary: A rectangle in float pixels, y down: the left edge at , the top at . A width or height of 0 or less makes it empty. Pixel (0, 0) covers the square from (0, 0) to (1, 1), so a rectangle with whole-number edges covers whole pixels.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.RoundRect
files.Summary: A rectangle with an x and y radius per corner. Radii that would overlap are scaled down together, as CSS and Skia do: every radius is multiplied by the smallest ratio of a side's length to the sum of the two radii along it, when that ratio is below 1. A radius below 0 counts as 0, and a corner with either radius 0 is square.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.RoundRectKind
files.Summary: What a reduces to, so backends and the rasterizer can take a shortcut.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.ShadowOptions
files.Summary: The light and colors of , after Skia's shadow model (the Material Design one): a shape lifted above the canvas casts an ambient shadow, blurred by its height, and a spot shadow from a round light at , moved away from the light and blurred by the light's size.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.SoftMask
files.Summary: A mask made by drawing, as a PDF soft mask: runs on a canvas of its own with the layer's transform and clip, and its alpha, or its luminosity over , through the optional curve, multiplies the layer. A luminosity mask of a white shape on black shows the layer only inside the shape.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.SoftMaskKind
files.Summary: Which value of a soft mask's drawing becomes the mask, as PDF's soft mask subtypes.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.SolidPaint
files.Summary: One color everywhere, with straight alpha. The color keeps float precision, so float and 16-bit targets get it in full; values outside 0 to 1 are kept on the paint, and the blend clamps them as Egami's Compositor does.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.SpriteTransform
files.Summary: A sprite's placement in , as Skia's RSXform: a rotation with a uniform scale, then a move. A point (x, y) of the sprite, measured from its source rectangle's top-left corner, goes to (ScaleCos·x − ScaleSin·y + Tx, ScaleSin·x + ScaleCos·y + Ty).

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.StampStyle
files.Summary: How places its shape along a path.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.Stroke
files.Summary: How a path is outlined: the pen's width, caps, joins and miter limit. The settings travel with the drawing call as data, so a vector backend can write them as they are (PDF's w, J, j and M). The pen is applied in the canvas's local space and then transformed, so a non-uniform scale gives an elliptical pen, as in PDF, SVG and Skia.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.SvgPathException
files.Summary: Thrown by when SVG path data breaks the grammar.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.SvgPathFormat
files.Summary: How writes SVG path data.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.SweepGradient
files.Summary: A gradient around a center, as Skia's sweep gradient and CSS's conic-gradient: t goes from 0 at to 1 at , in degrees clockwise (on a y-down screen) from the positive x axis.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.TextAnchor
files.Summary: Where text on a path is anchored at its start point, as SVG's text-anchor.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.TextOnPathOptions
files.Summary: How lays text along a path.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.TextPathSide
files.Summary: Which side of a path text stands on.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.TileMode
files.Summary: What a gradient or an image paint does past its ends or edges, as Skia's tile modes.

files.Title: Egami.Drawing.VerticalAlign
files.Summary: Where puts a paragraph across its lines, in a rectangle taller (or, for vertical lines, wider) than the lines.

files.Title: Egami.EgamiContext
files.Summary: Every setting that is not specific to one call: where memory comes from, how many threads an operation may use, and the safety limits. Contexts are immutable and safe to share. Change one with a with expression.

files.Title: Egami.EgamiDiagnostic
files.Summary: One event reported to , and the type of each entry in . Ids are listed in the diagnostics article and never renamed or reused.

files.Title: Egami.EgamiException
files.Summary: The base class of every exception Egami throws for problems with image data or limits.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.BitmapColorGlyph
files.Summary: An sbix or CBDT glyph: its image, the strike's size and where the image goes, in font units with y up, so it scales with the font; the drawing code decodes and resamples it.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.BitmapGlyphEncoding
files.Summary: The encoding of a bitmap glyph's image.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.CffOptions
files.Summary: What a bare CFF stream lacks and an sfnt would supply, for .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.CffStandardStrings
files.Summary: The Compact Font Format's predefined data (Adobe Technical Note #5176, appendices A and B): the 391 standard strings that string ids (SIDs) below 391 name, and the Standard and Expert encodings as glyph names by code.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.CharacterMap
files.Summary: One character map of a face, as stored: a cmap subtable for one (platform, encoding) pair, or a CFF font's own encoding as FreeType presents it (platform 7). Codes are the subtable's own: bytes for a Macintosh (1,0) map or a symbol font's (3,0) map, never translated to Unicode.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.CharacterMapping
files.Summary: A code and the glyph a gives it.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.CidSystemInfo
files.Summary: The character collection a CID-keyed font's CIDs belong to (its CFF ROS operator), such as Adobe-Japan1-7; PDF's CIDSystemInfo dictionary carries the same three values.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorCompositePaint
files.Summary: Two paints composited: the source onto the backdrop with a blend or Porter-Duff mode.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorExtend
files.Summary: What a color gradient does past the ends of its color line.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorGlyph
files.Summary: A glyph's color description from : a (COLR) or a (sbix, CBDT).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorGlyphFormats
files.Summary: The kinds of color glyph data a face holds.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorGlyphPaint
files.Summary: A paint clipped to a glyph's outline.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorGlyphReferencePaint
files.Summary: Another color glyph's paint graph drawn here, as COLR's PaintColrGlyph reuses it.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorLayersPaint
files.Summary: Paints drawn one over another, in order.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorLine
files.Summary: The stops of a color gradient and what happens past them.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorLinearGradientPaint
files.Summary: A linear gradient filling the clip: the color line runs from toward , with lines of equal color parallel to –, as COLR defines it.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorPaint
files.Summary: One node of a color glyph's paint graph, in font units with y up: COLR version 1 as OpenType 1.9.1 defines it (version 0 glyphs become layers of solid glyph fills), with variable values already taken at the face's position and palette colors resolved.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorRadialGradientPaint
files.Summary: A gradient between two circles filling the clip.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorSolidPaint
files.Summary: One color filling the clip.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorStop
files.Summary: A stop of a color line.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorSweepGradientPaint
files.Summary: A gradient around a center filling the clip, angles in degrees counter-clockwise from the x axis (y up).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.ColorTransformPaint
files.Summary: A paint under an affine transform in font units: COLR's transform, translate, scale, rotate and skew paints, each as its matrix (row vectors, y up).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Font
files.Summary: A typeface at a size: the em in canvas units (pixels on a raster, points on a PDF page). Scales the face's font-unit metrics and turns text into a positioned .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontCollection
files.Summary: A set of faces grouped into families: the caller's own, or for the fonts installed on the machine. Finds families by name and faces by style with the CSS Fonts Level 4 matching steps.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontEdging
files.Summary: How a glyph's edges are turned into pixels.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontEmbedding
files.Summary: The embedding permissions a face declares in its OS/2 fsType field. Egami reports them and never enforces them; a caller that embeds fonts, such as a PDF writer, decides what to do.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontExtents
files.Summary: A face's vertical metrics and decoration positions, with y up: in font units from , or in canvas units from .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontFamily
files.Summary: The faces of one family in a , matched by style.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontFileKind
files.Summary: What kind of font data some bytes hold, as sees it.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontHinting
files.Summary: How glyph outlines are fitted to the pixel grid before rasterizing.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontLoadOptions
files.Summary: How a font file is read: leniently with diagnostics (the default), or strictly.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontLoader
files.Summary: Tells what font data holds and loads every face of a collection.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontMatch
files.Summary: A matched face and the styling it lacks, from .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontNameRecord
files.Summary: One decoded string of a font's naming table, such as the family name in one language.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontOutlines
files.Summary: How a face stores its glyph outlines.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontPalette
files.Summary: The palette a color font draws with: a CPAL palette by index or by the background it suits, with entries overridden, as CSS's font-palette and .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontPaletteBackground
files.Summary: Which palettes prefers by the backgrounds CPAL says they suit.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontPaletteEntry
files.Summary: One palette entry replaced, as CSS's override-colors.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontPaletteInfo
files.Summary: One CPAL palette of a face.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontProbe
files.Summary: The result of .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontSlant
files.Summary: Whether a face is upright, italic or oblique.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontStyle
files.Summary: A face's style, or the style asked for when matching: weight from 1 to 1000 (400 normal, 700 bold), width from 1 to 9 (5 normal, as OS/2 usWidthClass), and slant.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontSubset
files.Summary: A font holding only some glyphs of another, from .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontSubsetter
files.Summary: Writes fonts that hold only the glyphs a document uses, as PDF embedding and SVG export want: TrueType, OpenType CFF or bare CFF, with composite glyphs and seac accents closed over and unused CFF subroutines dropped.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontSynthesis
files.Summary: Styling a face lacks, which a matched asks the renderer to synthesize (drawn from 2.7.2 on).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontTag
files.Summary: A four-byte OpenType tag, such as the table tag glyf or the feature tag kern.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.FontVariation
files.Summary: A position on one axis of a variable font, in the axis's own units, such as weight 650.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.GenericFamily
files.Summary: A generic family name, matched against fixed per-platform preference lists.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.GlyphColor
files.Summary: A color in a color glyph: a resolved palette color, or the foreground (palette entry 0xFFFF), which takes the paint's color and keeps only this color's alpha as a factor.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.GlyphExtents
files.Summary: A box around ink, such as a glyph's outline, with y up in font units or in a 's size.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.GlyphRun
files.Summary: Positioned glyphs of one font, ready to draw: glyph ids, one position per glyph relative to the run's origin (the first baseline's left end, y down, in canvas units), and optionally the source text with the UTF-16 index each glyph came from, which lets a PDF writer keep text searchable.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.GlyphTransform
files.Summary: A glyph's placement in a transformed : a rotation and uniform scale, then its origin, as Skia's RSXform. A point (x, y) of the glyph, y down, goes to (ScaleCos x - ScaleSin y + Tx, ScaleSin x + ScaleCos y + Ty).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.IColorPaintVisitor
files.Summary: Walks a color glyph's paint graph, one method per kind of node.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.IGlyphOutlineSink
files.Summary: Receives a glyph outline from , in font units with y up. Each contour starts with and ends with ; a closing line back to the start point is implied by and not sent.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.Caret
files.Summary: Where a caret is drawn: the primary segment, and at a bidi boundary, where the position touches text of both directions, a secondary segment at the other text's edge.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.CaretLine
files.Summary: A caret segment across the line: vertical in horizontal layouts, horizontal in vertical ones.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.CaretMove
files.Summary: How moves a caret.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.DecorationSegment
files.Summary: A piece of a decoration line along a text line: its left and right x.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.DecorationShape
files.Summary: One decoration line over a decorated stretch of one text line: an underline, overline or line-through at one position and thickness for the whole stretch (the lowest underline and thickest line among its fonts, as CSS), cut where glyphs cross an underline or overline when is Auto.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.ITextPaint
files.Summary: A paint that Egami.Fonts carries for text but never reads: Egami.Drawing's Paint implements it, so gradients, images and blend modes reach text drawn from a layout without Egami.Fonts depending on the drawing package.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LayoutRun
files.Summary: A piece of a line: glyphs of one font and bidi level, or a placeholder, tab or break.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LayoutRunKind
files.Summary: What a holds.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LineBreak
files.Summary: A place where a line may or must end.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LineBreakEnumerator
files.Summary: Enumerates line break opportunities; get one from .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LineBreakOptions
files.Summary: How text may break into lines, as CSS Text 3 sets it: word-break, overflow-wrap, line-break and the content language. The default is CSS's default: Unicode's line breaking algorithm (UAX #14) with breaks before small kana, as browsers break.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LineBreakStrictness
files.Summary: How strictly line breaks follow Chinese and Japanese rules (CSS line-break): breaks before small kana, hyphens, iteration marks and some punctuation.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LineBreaks
files.Summary: Finds where lines may break: Unicode's line breaking algorithm (UAX #14, Unicode 17.0) from Egami's own tables, with CSS Text 3's word-break and line-break switches. No shaping is involved, and there are no dictionaries: Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break only at spaces and zero width spaces.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LineFill
files.Summary: How lines are filled.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LineFlow
files.Summary: Lays a paragraph out one line at a time, each at its own width, so text can flow across columns and pages or around images; is built on it. Not thread-safe; make one per flow.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LineHeight
files.Summary: The height a run asks of its line box (CSS line-height): from the font's metrics, a of the font size or an height. The extra over the font's ascent and descent is split half above and half below.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.LineHeightKind
files.Summary: How a is given.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.OverflowWrap
files.Summary: Whether a piece wider than its line may break anywhere (CSS overflow-wrap).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.Paragraph
files.Summary: A paragraph of styled text, prepared once to be laid out at any width: styles resolved, bidi levels and break opportunities found, text itemized into runs and each run shaped. Immutable and safe to share between threads.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.ParagraphStyle
files.Summary: How a paragraph is laid out: its default text style, direction, alignment, line breaking, line filling, hyphens, ellipsis and line limits, line box rules, tabs and writing mode. The defaults follow CSS: start-aligned, greedy filling, normal line height, tab stops every 8 spaces, horizontal lines.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.Placeholder
files.Summary: An inline box laid out with the text, such as an icon or an image, which the caller draws: it stands for an object replacement character (U+FFFC) in the text, so bidi, line breaking and indexes treat it as one character.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.PlaceholderAlignment
files.Summary: How a sits on its line.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.RichText
files.Summary: Text with styles: a string, the s over it (sorted, never overlapping) and the s for its object replacement characters, in order. Immutable; build one with .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.RichTextBuilder
files.Summary: Builds a : a style, text, back to the enclosing style. Styles nest: a pushed style's unset fields come from the one it is pushed on, and the result has one flat span per stretch of equal style.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.SelectionHeight
files.Summary: How tall selection rectangles are.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.Strut
files.Summary: A minimum line box every line has, from a font and a line height (CSS's strut), or with the exact line box, for line grids in forms and columns.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.StyleSpan
files.Summary: A text style over a stretch of a , in UTF-16 units.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TabAlignment
files.Summary: How text aligns on a tab stop.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TabStop
files.Summary: An explicit tab stop.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextAffinity
files.Summary: Which side of a position a caret belongs to where one index has two places: at a line wrap or a bidi boundary.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextAlign
files.Summary: How lines align in their width (CSS text-align).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextAlignLast
files.Summary: How the last line, and lines before a hard break, align (CSS text-align-last).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextDecoration
files.Summary: Lines drawn with text (CSS Text Decoration 4).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextDecorationLines
files.Summary: Which decoration lines are drawn.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextDecorationSkipInk
files.Summary: Whether underlines and overlines skip glyph ink.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextDecorationStyle
files.Summary: How decoration lines are drawn.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextJustify
files.Summary: How justified lines stretch (CSS text-justify).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextLayout
files.Summary: A paragraph laid out at a width: its lines of glyph runs and the size of its layout box. Positions are in canvas units relative to the box's top-left corner, y down; nothing is rounded to pixels. Immutable and safe to share between threads.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextLine
files.Summary: One line of a laid-out paragraph: the text it holds, its line box and its runs in visual order. Coordinates are the layout box's, or for a line from a , the line's own box with its top at 0.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextOrientation
files.Summary: How characters stand in vertical lines (CSS text-orientation).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextPosition
files.Summary: A caret position: a UTF-16 index at a grapheme cluster boundary and the side it belongs to.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextShadow
files.Summary: A shadow under text: the glyphs and decorations again, moved and blurred (CSS text-shadow).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.TextStyle
files.Summary: How a stretch of text looks. Every field is optional: an unset field takes the enclosing builder style's, then the paragraph's , then Egami's default (16 pixels, black, normal line height, no decoration). Fields that change shaping (fonts, size, style, variations, language, features, letter spacing) split a paragraph into separately shaped runs; the others (colors, paints, background, decoration, shadows) never do, so a color change inside a ligature keeps the ligature.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.WordBreak
files.Summary: Where breaks may fall inside words (CSS word-break).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Layout.WritingMode
files.Summary: Whether lines run horizontally or vertically (CSS writing-mode).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.NamedInstance
files.Summary: A named instance of a variable font, such as "Bold Condensed", from its fvar table.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.OpticalSizing
files.Summary: Whether a sets a variable font's optical size axis from its size.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.PaintColorGlyph
files.Summary: A COLR glyph: its paint graph and, for version 1, the clip box the font gives.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.ClusterLevel
files.Summary: Which characters a glyph's cluster covers, as HarfBuzz's cluster levels.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.FontFallback
files.Summary: Where characters the font does not map go: the caller's font families first, matched to the font's style, then a resolver. Without fallback (, the default) shaping depends only on the fonts passed, never on the machine.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.FontFeature
files.Summary: An OpenType feature setting: a feature tag, a value and the range of UTF-16 units it applies to, in HarfBuzz's model. A value of 0 turns a feature off (such as default ligatures), 1 turns it on, and higher values pick an alternate.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.GlyphBuffer
files.Summary: A reusable buffer of shaped glyphs: glyph ids, the UTF-16 index of the text each came from, glyph flags and positions, in visual order. fills it; reuse one buffer for many runs to avoid allocations.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.GlyphFlags
files.Summary: What a shaped glyph says about breaking the text next to it, as HarfBuzz's glyph flags.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.GlyphPosition
files.Summary: How a shaped glyph moves the pen and sits relative to it, in the units of the it was shaped with.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.IFontFallbackResolver
files.Summary: Finds a face for a grapheme cluster no listed font maps, such as .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.OpenTypeLayout
files.Summary: What a face's OpenType layout tables (GSUB and GPOS) offer: the scripts, language systems and features they list, and the glyphs GSUB can produce from a set of glyphs. A table whose structure is damaged is left out whole, as the shaper leaves it out.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.RunProperties
files.Summary: What one run of text is shaped as: its script, language, direction, features and cluster level.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.ShapedLine
files.Summary: One line of : its range and its runs in visual order.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.ShapedRun
files.Summary: A run of a : one font, one bidi level, one script, one language, and its glyphs.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.ShapedText
files.Summary: Text shaped by : one per line between hard breaks, each with its runs in visual order. Nothing wraps.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.ShapingOptions
files.Summary: How shapes text: the paragraph direction, the language, script and features of the whole text, the fonts that take characters the font lacks, the cluster level, and styled spans.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.SystemFontFallback
files.Summary: The installed-font resolver of : fixed families for each script on Windows, macOS and Linux (Segoe UI Emoji, Apple Color Emoji or Noto Color Emoji for emoji; the language picks Japanese, Chinese or Korean faces for Han), then any installed face that maps the cluster, found once and remembered for the process.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.TextShaper
files.Summary: OpenType text shaping in managed code: a run of text in one font becomes positioned glyphs with GSUB substitutions, GPOS positioning and the script rules HarfBuzz applies.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Shaping.TextSpan
files.Summary: A range of text with its own font, language or features, for .

files.Summary: What writes.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.SubsetOptions
files.Summary: How writes a subset.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.TextBounds
files.Summary: A box in canvas units with y down, such as the ink of a relative to its origin.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.TextMeasure
files.Summary: The size of text as lays it out, in canvas units.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Typeface
files.Summary: One font face: its names, style, metrics, character map, glyph outlines and kerning, read from a TrueType or OpenType font, a collection, or a bare CFF stream. Immutable and safe to share across threads, canvases and backends.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.Bidi

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.BidiClass
files.Summary: A code point's Bidi_Class (UAX #9).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.BidiPairedBracketType
files.Summary: A code point's Bidi_Paired_Bracket_Type.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.BidiResult
files.Summary: The result of : a level per UTF-16 unit, the runs in logical order, and the visual order of any line. Dispose it to return its arrays to the pool.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.BidiRun
files.Summary: A run of UTF-16 units at one embedding level.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.EastAsianWidth
files.Summary: A code point's East_Asian_Width (UAX #11).

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.GraphemeEnumerator
files.Summary: Enumerates extended grapheme clusters; get one from .

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.JoiningGroup
files.Summary: A code point's Joining_Group, the letter shape family of an Arabic or Syriac letter.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.JoiningType
files.Summary: A code point's Joining_Type, which drives cursive joining in Arabic, Syriac, N'Ko, Mongolian and similar scripts.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.LineBreakClass
files.Summary: A code point's Line_Break class (UAX #14), which line breaking starts from.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.Script
files.Summary: A Unicode script, such as Latin, Arabic or Devanagari, with its ISO 15924 code and the OpenType script tags fonts use for it.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.TextDirection
files.Summary: The direction of a paragraph or a run of text.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.TextSegment
files.Summary: A range of UTF-16 units: a grapheme cluster, a word or a run.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.TextSegmenter
files.Summary: Text boundaries from UAX #29: extended grapheme clusters (what a reader sees as one character) and words, with Unicode's default rules and no dictionaries.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.UnicodeData
files.Summary: The Unicode character properties text shaping needs, from Egami's own tables generated from the Unicode Character Database (version ), so results never move with the .NET runtime's Unicode version.

files.Title: Egami.Fonts.Unicode.VerticalOrientation
files.Summary: A code point's Vertical_Orientation (UAX #50): upright or rotated in vertical text.

files.Summary: Options for reading raw CCITT data: its parameters, which the data cannot carry itself.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.IFormatReader
files.Summary: Reads one file format. Readers are stateless and safe to share across threads. They read only through and allocate pixel memory only through , which checks the safety limits first, so no reader can allocate before the size has been checked.

files.Summary: Writes one file format. Writers are stateless, safe to share across threads, and never change the raster they are given.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.IRowFormatReader
files.Summary: An optional interface for a format's reader: an open image that hands out rows as they are asked for, so streams the format, with and applied on the way out. A reader without it still works everywhere: the decoder reads the whole image with and serves rows from it. Load, Probe and an incremental decode keep using .

files.Title: Egami.Formats.IRowFormatWriter
files.Summary: An optional interface for a format's writer: an encoder that takes rows and frames one at a time. A writer that implements it streams through and , and and SaveAsync use it in place of , so all of them write the same bytes. A writer without it still works everywhere: the encoder gathers the image and calls at the end.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Ico.CurFormat
files.Summary: The Windows cursor format, registered in : an icon whose entries also carry a hotspot, the pixel that points. Read and written as , with and .

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Ico.IcoDetails
files.Summary: Details only ICO and CUR have, kept in .

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Ico.IcoEntry
files.Summary: One entry of an icon's directory, as read from the entry's own header.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Ico.IcoEntryEncoding
files.Summary: How an icon entry's pixels are stored.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Ico.IcoFormat
files.Summary: The Windows icon format, registered in . An icon holds several images (entries), each a PNG file or a BMP without its file header. Load returns the best entry, LoadAll every entry, and Save writes one entry per raster or a set resized to .

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Ico.IcoReaderOptions

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Ico.IcoWriterOptions
files.Summary: Options for writing ICO and CUR. Each raster becomes one entry at its own size, or one entry per size in ; entries are 8-bit RGBA, sorted smallest first. EXIF, XMP and IPTC are not written; an ICC profile goes into PNG entries.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Jbig2.Jbig2CombinationOperator

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransformEdges
files.Summary: What a lossless transform does with the blocks at the right or bottom edge when the image is not a whole number of MCUs (8 or 16 pixels) across or down, so those blocks cannot move to the other side intact.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransformOperation

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransformOptions

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransformResult

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegWriterOptions

files.Title: Egami.Formats.RecoveryMode

files.Title: Egami.Formats.RowEncoder<TPixel>
files.Summary: One encode in progress: a still image's rows top-down with , or whole frames with , then .

files.Title: Egami.Formats.RowReader<TNatural>
files.Summary: An open image whose natural pixel type is TNatural, as would give it.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.RowReader
files.Summary: One open image, as a format reader streams it: frames of rows at the stored size. Derive from , which names the natural pixel type.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.SignatureMatcher
files.Summary: Returns whether the first bytes of a file belong to a format.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tga.TgaAlphaType
files.Summary: The TGA 2.0 alpha type from the extension area.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tga.TgaOrigin
