files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tga.TgaPixelFormat
files.Summary: The pixel layout a TGA is written with.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tga.TgaWriterOptions
files.Summary: Options for writing TGA.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffByteOrder
files.Summary: The byte order of a TIFF file.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffCompression
files.Summary: A TIFF compression scheme, by its code in the Compression tag.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffDetails
files.Summary: Details only TIFF has, kept per page in .

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffExtraSample
files.Summary: What an extra sample is, from the ExtraSamples tag.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffFormat
files.Summary: The TIFF format, registered in .

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffLayout
files.Summary: Classic TIFF, with 32-bit offsets and a 4 GB limit, or BigTIFF, with 64-bit offsets.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffPhotometric
files.Summary: What a page's samples mean, from the PhotometricInterpretation tag.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffPredictor
files.Summary: The horizontal differencing applied before LZW or Deflate, from the Predictor tag.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffReaderOptions
files.Summary: Options for reading TIFF.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffSampleFormat
files.Summary: How a page's samples are numbers, from the SampleFormat tag.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffTag
files.Summary: A TIFF tag Egami does not map, kept as it was read so the TIFF writer can write it back: GeoTIFF, DNG and private tags.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Tiff.TiffWriterOptions
files.Summary: Options for writing TIFF.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Webp.Vp8FrameInfo
files.Summary: What a VP8 frame was, as returns it.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Webp.Vp8StreamDecoder
files.Summary: Decodes a VP8 video stream (RFC 6386) a frame at a time, as WebM and IVF files carry it: key frames and inter frames, with the last, golden and alternate references, motion vectors and hidden frames. The frames equal libvpx's sample for sample. Feed the frames in stream order; decoding starts at a key frame. Containers are not read here: Egami.Video reads WebM and IVF and uses this decoder, and any other source of VP8 frames can too.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Webp.WebpChunk
files.Summary: A chunk Egami does not read itself, kept unchanged for round trips.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Webp.WebpChunkPosition
files.Summary: Where a kept chunk sat in a WebP file, so it can be written back in the same place.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Webp.WebpDetails
files.Summary: Details only WebP has, kept in so a WebP can be written back as it was.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Webp.WebpFormat
files.Summary: The WebP format, registered in : lossless (VP8L), lossy (VP8) with or without alpha, and animated.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Webp.WebpFrameDetails
files.Summary: Details of one frame of an animated WebP, kept in . Delay, blending, disposal and the frame's rectangle are in .

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Webp.WebpReaderOptions
files.Summary: Options for reading WebP, on top of the general .

files.Title: Egami.Formats.Webp.WebpWriterOptions
files.Summary: Options for writing WebP. The defaults follow libwebp's: quality 75 and effort (libwebp's method) 4. A raster read from a WebP file keeps its kind, lossless or lossy; anything else is written lossy.

files.Title: Egami.Formats.WriterOptions
files.Summary: Options for writing. Each format has a subclass with its own settings; writers given this base class use their defaults.

files.Title: Egami.Frame<TPixel>
files.Summary: One frame of a raster: a pixel plane the size of the raster plus per-frame metadata.

files.Title: Egami.FrameList<TPixel>
files.Summary: The frames of a raster, all the same size and pixel type. There is always at least one. Frames added from anywhere are copied, so a frame belongs to one raster only.

files.Title: Egami.IPixelMemorySource
files.Summary: Supplies the memory behind every . Implement it to control where pixel memory comes from. Implementations must be thread-safe.

files.Title: Egami.InkCoverage
files.Summary: How much ink an prints, from .

files.Title: Egami.InkDepth
files.Summary: How many bits each plane of an stores per pixel.

files.Title: Egami.InkPlate
files.Summary: One plane of an : an ink's plate, or the alpha plane. Rows are read and written in place; shows the plane as a gray raster without copying.

files.Title: Egami.InkRaster
files.Summary: A printed page as plates: one plane per ink of an (a disabled spot has none) plus one alpha plane, each 8 or 16 bits. A plane holds the ink as it prints over paper, 0 for none to the depth's maximum for full ink: drawing translucently leaves less ink, so the planes are premultiplied by the alpha plane, and a plate is ready to print as it is. A new raster is blank: no ink, alpha 0.

files.Title: Egami.InkTiffOptions
files.Summary: How an is saved as a separated TIFF.

files.Title: Egami.LimitExceededException
files.Summary: Thrown when a limit is exceeded.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.ColorSpaceHint
files.Summary: What the raster's pixel values mean, as far as the file said.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.ExifData
files.Summary: A parsed EXIF block (a TIFF structure, CIPA DC-008): the tags of IFD0, the EXIF, GPS and interoperability sub-IFDs and IFD1 with its thumbnail, with typed getters for the common ones. An unedited block writes back byte for byte; after an edit it is laid out again, keeping the maker note at its old offset when it fits, since maker notes often hold offsets of their own.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.ExifEntry
files.Summary: One EXIF value: its tag, TIFF type and raw bytes, with accessors that read them as text, integers or fractions.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.ExifFraction
files.Summary: A rational EXIF value, such as an exposure time of 1/250 or an aperture of 28/10.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.ExifIfd
files.Summary: The image file directories (IFDs) an EXIF block holds its tags in.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.ExifKey
files.Summary: An EXIF tag: its number and the IFD it lives in. The named keys cover the tags most programs read and write.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.ExifType
files.Summary: The TIFF data types EXIF values are stored as.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.FormatDetails
files.Summary: Format-specific details the reader found, such as the original color type or palette. Each format derives its own.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.FrameBlend
files.Summary: How a frame is combined with what is already on the canvas.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.FrameDisposal
files.Summary: What happens to a frame's area before the next frame is drawn.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.FrameMetadata
files.Summary: Metadata that belongs to one frame.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.GeoPosition
files.Summary: A position from the GPS tags of an EXIF block.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.ImageOrientation
files.Summary: How stored pixels must be turned to show the image upright: the EXIF Orientation tag (274). The value says which way the camera was held; AutoOrient applies it.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.IptcData
files.Summary: Parsed IPTC-IIM datasets (IPTC-IIM 4.2), as news agencies, stock libraries and Lightroom write them next to XMP, with typed getters for the common ones. Shaped like : an unedited block writes back byte for byte; after an edit it is rebuilt in record and dataset order, record 1 first, with the coded character set (1:90) set to UTF-8 whenever a value is not plain ASCII.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.IptcEntry
files.Summary: One IPTC-IIM dataset as stored: its key and its bytes.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.IptcKey
files.Summary: An IPTC-IIM dataset: its record and dataset numbers, as "2:25" for keywords. The named keys cover the datasets news, stock and photo software read and write; any other pair works too.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.RasterMetadata
files.Summary: Metadata that belongs to the whole raster. It is kept apart from the pixels and survives operations unless an operation makes it wrong. Metadata problems never fail a load: broken blocks are kept as bytes and noted in .

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.Resolution
files.Summary: Physical pixel density.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.ResolutionUnit
files.Summary: The unit of a .

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.TextEntry
files.Summary: A text entry, such as a PNG text chunk or a GIF comment.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.XmpArray
files.Summary: An XMP array: items in order, each a simple value (), an or another , with a language for the items of a language alternative.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.XmpArrayKind
files.Summary: The three kinds of XMP array.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.XmpData
files.Summary: A parsed XMP packet: its properties by namespace URI and local name, each a simple value, an or an , with typed getters and setters for what apps ask for most (Dublin Core, XMP Basic, Photoshop and TIFF properties). An unedited packet writes back byte for byte; an edited one is written as canonical RDF/XML with padding, keeping every property it does not know, qualifiers included.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.XmpName
files.Summary: An XMP property name: a namespace URI and a local name, such as dc:title. Prefixes vary between files, so Egami never matches on them; holds the URIs of the common schemas.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.XmpNamespaces
files.Summary: The namespace URIs of the XMP schemas apps use most.

files.Title: Egami.Metadata.XmpStruct
files.Summary: An XMP structure: named fields, each a simple value (), an or another , such as Iptc4xmpCore:CreatorContactInfo. holds its top-level properties the same way.

files.Title: Egami.Metafiles.Metafile
files.Summary: A Windows metafile, WMF, EMF or EMF+ (and their gzip forms WMZ and EMZ), read and checked; its records stay internal (design question 3). The size facts come from the header: an EMF's frame, a placeable WMF's box and units per inch, or a plain WMF's window extent at 96 DPI. A metafile is immutable and safe to read from many threads.

files.Title: Egami.Metafiles.MetafileDecodeOptions
files.Summary: How draws a metafile for Raster.Load and sizes it for Raster.Probe.

files.Title: Egami.Metafiles.MetafileFormat
files.Summary: WMF, EMF and EMF+ (and WMZ, EMZ) as an Egami format: registered with , Raster.Load draws a metafile at its own size at 96 DPI (or ) onto a transparent raster, and Raster.Probe gives that size from the header without drawing. Text uses the installed fonts. For your own fonts, a target size, a background or the GDI part of a dual file, load a and call .

files.Title: Egami.Metafiles.MetafileKind
files.Summary: What a holds.

files.Title: Egami.Metafiles.MetafileLoadOptions
files.Summary: How reads a file: which limits and diagnostics apply.

files.Title: Egami.Metafiles.MetafilePlayback
files.Summary: Which records of an EMF+ dual file play.

files.Title: Egami.Metafiles.MetafileRenderOptions
files.Summary: How and draw a metafile.

files.Title: Egami.MipChain
files.Summary: A chain of ever-halved copies of an image, for making many smaller sizes fast: each resize starts from the smallest level that is still at least twice the target, so a gallery of thumbnail sizes reads each source pixel about once instead of once per size. Level 0 is the source itself; each next level halves the size, rounding up, by averaging 2 × 2 blocks of premultiplied pixels.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.Anchor
files.Summary: Where an image sits inside a larger area, or which part of it is kept when it is cut down.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.AnimationOverlayOptions
files.Summary: Options for .

files.Title: Egami.Operations.AnimationTiming
files.Summary: How pairs the overlay's frames with the base's.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.BlendMode
files.Summary: How a source color is combined with the destination under it: the twelve Porter–Duff operators, Plus and Modulate, and the separable and non-separable blend modes of the W3C Compositing and Blending specification, plus Add and Subtract. Blend modes ( to ) blend the colors where both are present, then composite source-over. The values are fixed: they never change between releases.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.BlurMethod
files.Summary: How computes a Gaussian blur.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ChannelSource
files.Summary: Where an output channel of takes its value from.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ColorChannel
files.Summary: One channel of a raster's working RGBA, or its luminance, for .

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ColorChannels
files.Summary: A set of a raster's working RGBA channels, for .

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ColorFilter
files.Summary: A function of one pixel's color, as a value: build one from a matrix, curves, a 3D table or a tone step, chain filters with , mix two with , run one with or on your own pixels with , and save it as a .cube file through . Like Skia's SkColorFilter, a filter sees only the pixel's own straight RGBA: no neighbours, position or image statistics, so any chain of filters runs as one pass.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ColorMatrix
files.Summary: A 4 × 5 color matrix applied to straight (not premultiplied) RGBA scaled to 0..1: each output channel is m[row, 0] × R + m[row, 1] × G + m[row, 2] × B + m[row, 3] × A + m[row, 4], rows in R, G, B, A order, and results are clamped to 0..1. The factories follow the W3C Filter Effects definitions.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ColorSpace
files.Summary: The color space in which resizing, blurs and grayscale blend colors: the stored sRGB-encoded values, or linear light.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ColorVisionDeficiency
files.Summary: A color vision deficiency to simulate.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.Compositor
files.Summary: Blends rows of pixels with a , for code that composites outside an operation chain: a custom , a rasterizer filling spans, a layer merge. It runs the kernels DrawImage runs, so on a row gives the pixels DrawImage gives there. Every method works for every pixel type, allocates nothing once warm, and is safe to call from many threads at once.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.Connectivity
files.Summary: Which neighbours a flood fill spreads to.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ContrastInvert
files.Summary: How inverts, as Skia's high-contrast filter does.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ConvolutionKernel
files.Summary: A convolution kernel: an odd width and height of weights, applied as laid out (the weight at column 0, row 0 multiplies the pixel up and to the left of the center). The sum is divided by and is added to the color channels.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.CubeFile
files.Summary: Reads and writes .cube LUT files: the Adobe Cube LUT Specification 1.0 (a 1D or a 3D table, with TITLE, DOMAIN_MIN and DOMAIN_MAX), and DaVinci Resolve's variant with a 1D shaper before the 3D table (LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE and LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE).

files.Title: Egami.Operations.DistantLight
files.Summary: A light infinitely far away, shining from one direction on every pixel, as SVG's feDistantLight. The direction toward the light is (cos · cos , sin · cos , sin ) in the raster's coordinates (y down), which is the vector Skia's DistantLit factories take.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.DropShadowOptions
files.Summary: The less common settings of : a different vertical blur, whether the canvas grows, whether only the shadow is kept, and how the blur is computed.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.EdgeMode
files.Summary: How a convolution reads taps that fall past the image border.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.EdgeOperator
files.Summary: The kernels finds edges with. Every operator is scaled so a full black-to-white step gives 1 at its strongest pixel; stronger responses (corners, single bright pixels) clamp to 1.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.EqualizeMode
files.Summary: What equalizes.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.HeightSource
files.Summary: Which channel reads as the surface's height.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.Homography
files.Summary: A 3 × 3 projective matrix in double precision, for perspective transforms. It follows 's conventions: points are row vectors, so [x, y, 1] × H = [X, Y, W] and the point lands at (X / W, Y / W); A * B applies A first, then B. Coordinates are in pixels with the origin at the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, so pixel centers sit at +0.5.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.IRasterOperation
files.Summary: One step of an operation chain. Built-in operations implement it, and so can callers: add one to a chain with .

files.Title: Egami.Operations.IWarp
files.Summary: A general warp: a mapping from each output pixel back to the source point it shows. Egami samples the points with the same sampler as , so every warp gets antialiasing where it shrinks the image, and edge modes. Positions are in pixels with the origin at the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, so pixel centers sit at +0.5.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.LensBlurOptions
files.Summary: The aperture and highlights of . The defaults give a round aperture in linear light with no highlight boost.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.Light
files.Summary: A light for : , or , the three light sources of the SVG 1.1 lighting filters (feDistantLight, fePointLight and feSpotLight), with Skia's parameters. Positions are in pixels of the raster, x to the right, y down and z up out of the image; a pixel's center is at (x + 0.5, y + 0.5), as in Skia.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.LightingModel
files.Summary: How a surface reflects light in : (SVG's feDiffuseLighting, Lambert's N·L) or (feSpecularLighting, Phong–Blinn's (N·H)^shininess), with SVG's and Skia's constants.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.LightingOptions
files.Summary: The surface and output settings of .

files.Title: Egami.Operations.LumaWeights
files.Summary: The luma weights a grayscale conversion uses.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.Lut3D
files.Summary: A 3D color lookup table: an N × N × N grid of output RGB values over the input cube, with red varying fastest, as .cube files and Hald images store it, and an optional 1D shaper per channel read before the grid (DaVinci Resolve's 1D-plus-3D .cube). Read one with or , and apply it with .

files.Title: Egami.Operations.LutInterpolation
files.Summary: How a reads between its grid points.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.Mask
files.Summary: A raster read as coverage, 0 (none) to full, placed on the image being edited: where an operation inside applies and how strongly. The raster may have any size and pixel type; outside it coverage is 0, or full when . Its first frame is used for every frame. It must stay undisposed until the chain has run.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.MaskChannel
files.Summary: Which values of a raster a reads as coverage.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.MorphologyOp
files.Summary: The operations of , all flat (gray-level) and per channel.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.NoiseKind
files.Summary: The noise adds: ImageMagick's +noise kinds, with values on 0..1 and the amount as ImageMagick's -attenuate. At amount 1 the formulas are ImageMagick's Q16 ones.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.OperationInput<TPixel>
files.Summary: Everything an operation gets for one frame.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.OperationReach
files.Summary: How far an operation chain reads past each output pixel, in whole pixels across and down: a pixel of the result can depend on input pixels up to columns and rows away. A blur of σ reaches about 3σ; a color matrix reaches nothing. measures a chain, so code that runs one on part of a larger picture, such as a canvas layer, can include the pixels around it that the chain will read.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.PixelMath
files.Summary: An arithmetic operation with a constant, for : ImageMagick's -evaluate operators.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.PointLight
files.Summary: A light at one point, shining in every direction, as SVG's fePointLight and Skia's PointLit factories.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.RasterOps
files.Summary: Animation steps: they work on the frames of the whole animation rather than on each frame, so they run in Apply, Derive and Transcode (which then decodes the whole animation first) but not inside Within. Frames in memory are already full pictures of what is on screen, so there is no Coalesce, and the writers find each frame's changed area themselves, so there is no Optimize.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ResampleFilter
files.Summary: The kernel a resize or rotation uses to blend source pixels.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.RowBandAction
files.Summary: Processes a band of rows: rows start (inclusive) to end (exclusive).

files.Title: Egami.Operations.SamplingOptions
files.Summary: How a transform or warp samples the source: the filter, the color space it blends in, what samples outside the source read, and the background color.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.SpotLight
files.Summary: A light at one point that shines toward a target, as SVG's feSpotLight and Skia's SpotLit factories. Light falls off away from the axis as cos(angle)^ and stops at , with Skia's soft cone edge.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.StackMode
files.Summary: How combines the same channel of the same pixel across rasters.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.StructuringElement
files.Summary: The shape takes its maximum or minimum over: a set of cells around an origin, which sits on the pixel being computed. The factories make the shapes ImageMagick's -morphology kernels of the same names make (its Plus is here). The default value is the origin alone, which changes nothing.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ThresholdMethod
files.Summary: How and choose a level from the histogram.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ThresholdMode
files.Summary: What a threshold compares with its level.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.ToneCurve
files.Summary: A curve from 0..1 to 0..1 for one channel, as a photo editor's curves dialog draws it: inputs outside 0..1 are clamped first and results are clamped to 0..1. Use one in ; the tone steps (Level, Gamma and the rest) are curves too, evaluated exactly.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.TransformOptions
files.Summary: How a transform samples the source and how large its result is: plus a viewport.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.Warp
files.Summary: Makes warps from functions.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.Warps
files.Summary: The built-in warps for : lens correction, polar and depolar, arc, swirl, wave and implode with ImageMagick's parameter meanings, so its documentation describes them and its results are their reference, and Skia's magnifier. Positions are in pixels with pixel centers at +0.5.

files.Title: Egami.Operations.WhiteBalanceMethod
files.Summary: How finds the cast to remove.

files.Title: Egami.PixelMemoryLeakEventArgs
files.Summary: Describes a pixel memory block that was collected without being disposed.

files.Title: Egami.PixelMemoryUsage
files.Summary: What a has handed out and not yet had back, and opt-in tracking of blocks that were never disposed. Get it from ; most callers want PooledPixelMemorySource.Shared.Usage.

files.Title: Egami.PixelPlane<TPixel>
files.Summary: A width × height grid of pixels, stored row by row. A row is always one contiguous span, but the plane as a whole may be split into several blocks of whole rows. Planes belong to the raster or operation that hands them out, which returns their memory; user code reads and writes them but never frees them.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Abgr8
files.Summary: A pixel with 8-bit alpha, blue, green and red channels, in that order, with straight alpha. Matches the bytes of a little-endian 32-bit RGBA value read as an integer.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Alpha8
files.Summary: A pixel with one 8-bit alpha channel: a mask, or glyph coverage. As a color it is black with that alpha; converting a color to it keeps only the alpha, so a type without alpha gives 255.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.AlphaKind
files.Summary: How a pixel type stores alpha.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Argb8
files.Summary: A pixel with 8-bit alpha, red, green and blue channels, in that order, with straight alpha. Matches the byte order of big-endian ARGB buffers, such as Java's and some TIFF and PSD files.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Bgr565
files.Summary: A 16-bit packed pixel: blue in bits 0 to 4, green in bits 5 to 10, red in bits 11 to 15, and no alpha. The same memory as Skia's and Android's RGB 565 and the 16-bit BMP 5-6-5 bit field. Widening and narrowing both round to the nearest value, so every 16-bit value survives a round trip through .

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Bgr8
files.Summary: A pixel with 8-bit blue, green and red channels, in that order, and no alpha.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Bgra4444
files.Summary: A 16-bit packed pixel: blue in bits 0 to 3, green in 4 to 7, red in 8 to 11 and straight alpha in 12 to 15. The same memory as the DXGI and Vulkan B4G4R4A4 formats. Each level widens to 8 bits by multiplying by 17, and narrowing rounds to nearest.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Bgra8
files.Summary: A pixel with 8-bit blue, green, red and straight alpha channels, in that order.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.ChromaFormat
files.Summary: How a stores chroma: at what resolution against luma, or not at all.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.ChromaSiting
files.Summary: Where each chroma sample of a or picture sits against the luma samples it covers. Conversions filter chroma to match, so colors line up with edges. Ignored for 4:4:4 and 4:0:0.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Cmyk16
files.Summary: A pixel with 16-bit cyan, magenta, yellow and black ink amounts, in that order, 0 meaning no ink. 16-bit CMYK TIFF and PSD.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Cmyk8
files.Summary: A pixel with 8-bit cyan, magenta, yellow and black ink amounts, in that order, 0 meaning no ink. CMYK JPEG, TIFF and PSD.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Gray16
files.Summary: A pixel with one 16-bit luminance channel and no alpha.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Gray8
files.Summary: A pixel with one 8-bit luminance channel and no alpha.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.GrayAlpha16
files.Summary: A pixel with 16-bit luminance and straight alpha channels, in that order.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.GrayAlpha8
files.Summary: A pixel with 8-bit luminance and straight alpha channels, in that order.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.GrayF32
files.Summary: A pixel with one 32-bit float luminance channel, nominally 0 to 1, and no alpha: PFM gray maps, depth and height maps.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.IPixelType<TSelf>
files.Summary: A pixel type: an unmanaged struct holding one pixel. The conversions (ToScaled, FromScaled, ToRgba8, FromRgba8) always use sRGB-encoded values with straight (not premultiplied) alpha; says how the pixel is stored, so Egami can take faster paths for layouts it knows. Types from outside Egami may use any layout, with for ones Egami does not know.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.PixelChannelOrder
files.Summary: The order in which a pixel type stores its channels.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.PixelChannelType
files.Summary: The storage type of every channel in a pixel type.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.PixelConvert
files.Summary: Converts spans of pixels from one pixel type to another.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.PixelLayoutInfo
files.Summary: Describes the memory layout of a pixel type.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.PremulBgra8
files.Summary: A pixel with 8-bit blue, green and red channels premultiplied by the alpha channel, in that order: the layout of Windows and GPU surfaces.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.PremulRgba8
files.Summary: A pixel with 8-bit red, green and blue channels premultiplied by the alpha channel, in that order: Skia's N32 premultiplied.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.PremulRgbaF32
files.Summary: A pixel with 32-bit float red, green and blue channels premultiplied by the alpha channel, in that order, for float compositing and blending. The conversions take and return straight colors; values are not clamped, except that a premultiplied pixel with zero alpha has no color.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Rgb10A2
files.Summary: A 32-bit packed pixel: red in bits 0 to 9, green in 10 to 19, blue in 20 to 29 and straight alpha in 30 and 31. The same memory as the DXGI R10G10B10A2 and Vulkan A2B10G10R10 formats, used by 10-bit displays. Ten-bit levels round to the nearest 16-bit value and convert through exactly; two-bit alpha widens by multiplying.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Rgb16
files.Summary: A pixel with 16-bit red, green and blue channels, in that order, and no alpha.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Rgb8
files.Summary: A pixel with 8-bit red, green and blue channels, in that order, and no alpha.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.RgbF32
files.Summary: A pixel with 32-bit float red, green and blue channels, in that order, nominally 0 to 1, and no alpha.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Rgba16
files.Summary: A pixel with 16-bit red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.Rgba8
files.Summary: A pixel with 8-bit red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order. Egami's default working type.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.RgbaF16
files.Summary: A pixel with 16-bit float () red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order, nominally 0 to 1. Values outside 0..1 (HDR) are kept until written to an integer type; conversion to and from rounds as (Half)f does: to nearest even, with values above 65,504 becoming infinity.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.RgbaF32
files.Summary: A pixel with 32-bit float red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order, nominally 0 to 1.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.YuvColor
files.Summary: How the samples of a turn into RGB: the matrix, the range and where chroma sits. Every load, wrap and conversion states one, so a picture is never read with a guessed matrix.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.YuvMatrix
files.Summary: The matrix between RGB and luma-chroma (Y'CbCr) values, as ITU-T H.273 names them. Shared by and planar YUV images, so their coefficients never disagree.

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.YuvPackedFormat
files.Summary: The interleaved YUV layouts that operating system decoders, GPUs and webcams hand out, which a copies to and from its planes with and .

files.Title: Egami.Pixels.YuvRange
files.Summary: Whether luma-chroma values use the whole range or the video range.

files.Title: Egami.Point
files.Summary: A position in pixels. X grows to the right and Y downward; the top-left pixel is (0, 0).

files.Title: Egami.PooledPixelMemorySource
files.Summary: The default . Small blocks are arrays rented from a shared pool; larger blocks are unmanaged memory aligned to 64 bytes, which stays off the large object heap and suits SIMD. Planes larger than are split into several blocks of whole rows.

files.Title: Egami.ProofOptions
files.Summary: How shows the plates on screen.

files.Title: Egami.Quantization.DitherMode
files.Summary: How the error of mapping pixels to a palette is spread: error diffusion (Floyd–Steinberg and eight other published kernels, and Riemersma's Hilbert-curve walk) or an ordered pattern (Bayer 2, 4, 8 and 16, and 3 × 3). The values are fixed.

files.Title: Egami.Quantization.ErrorDiffusionKernel
files.Summary: A custom error-diffusion kernel for : how much of each pixel's error goes to which neighbours. Row 0 of is the current row, with the current pixel at column ; the following rows are the rows below. Only entries to the right of the current pixel on row 0, and every entry below, may be non-zero, since the rest have been mapped already.

files.Title: Egami.Quantization.IndexedImage
files.Summary: An image as palette indices: one byte per pixel and the palette they index, for formats and APIs that want indexed color, such as a PDF indexed image. The indices are pooled; dispose the image to return them.

files.Title: Egami.Quantization.Palette
files.Summary: An ordered list of up to 256 colors to map images onto: a brand palette, a display's inks, or one built from an image with Wu's quantizer. Use it as for the GIF, PNG, BMP and TGA writers, with , or to find the nearest color yourself.

files.Title: Egami.Quantization.PaletteOptions
files.Summary: How formats with at most 256 colors (GIF, PNG with a palette, and indexed BMP and TGA) build their palette when an image has more colors than fit. Images with few enough colors always keep them exactly, without dithering.

files.Title: Egami.Quantization.Palettes
files.Summary: Ready-made palettes.

files.Title: Egami.Raster<TPixel>
files.Summary: An image whose pixels are of type TPixel. Pixel access is by row span.

files.Title: Egami.Raster
files.Summary: Measuring images: comparison, statistics, histograms, colors and a pixel signature. Nothing here changes a raster.

files.Title: Egami.RasterDecoder
files.Summary: One open image, decoded a band of rows or a frame at a time. Opening reads the header and the metadata that comes before the image data; and then hand out the image in any pixel type, with and applied as in .

files.Title: Egami.RasterEncoder<TPixel>
files.Summary: An image being written a band of rows or a frame at a time, so a huge image never has to exist whole. The bytes are the ones writes for the same pixels and options, except where a format must write differently without seeking: top-down BMP and TGA rows, and run-length TGA, which is always top-down. Options that need every pixel before the first byte (automatic palettes, PNG's Reduce, automatic alpha) throw at Create instead of quietly writing something else.

files.Title: Egami.RasterEncoder
files.Summary: Creates a , which writes an image a band of rows or a frame at a time.

files.Title: Egami.RasterList
files.Summary: The images of a file that holds several, each its own raster with its own size, pixel type and metadata: a TIFF's pages, an icon's entries. The list owns them: disposing it disposes every raster.

files.Title: Egami.Rect
files.Summary: A rectangle of pixels: the top-left corner and a size.

files.Title: Egami.RowAction<TPixel>
files.Summary: Processes one row of pixels.

files.Title: Egami.SafetyLimits
files.Summary: Limits that protect against hostile or broken files. Readers check sizes from the header before allocating any pixel memory. The defaults let normal photos and screenshots through. Change them with a with expression.

files.Title: Egami.Size
files.Summary: A width and height in pixels.

files.Title: Egami.SpritePackOptions
files.Summary: How lays sprites out.

files.Title: Egami.SpriteSheet
files.Summary: A sprite sheet: many images packed into one, with the rectangle of each. Packing uses the MaxRects algorithm with the best short side fit (Jylänki, "A Thousand Ways to Pack the Bin", 2010), the images taken by height, tallest first, and then by input order, so the same inputs always give the same sheet. Sprites are never rotated.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgAttribute
files.Summary: An attribute of an : its name, namespace, the prefix it was written with, and its value.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgAttributeCollection
files.Summary: An element's attributes, in file order. Setting, adding and removing mark the document's render tree for rebuilding.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgCanvas
files.Summary:
A canvas that writes SVG: every drawing call becomes SVG elements, so anything drawn on a (shapes, strokes, gradients, images, text, clips, layers, recorded pictures) can be saved as a vector file that browsers, Inkscape and Egami.Svg all read. Gradients, patterns, clips, masks, images, glyph outlines and pictures are written once in defs and shared. What SVG cannot express (sweep gradients, noise and composed paints, meshes, layers with filters) is drawn by Egami into an image at and embedded as PNG.

The output is SVG 1.1 with CSS mix-blend-mode and isolation for blend modes and layers (and SVG 2's fr for a conical gradient whose start circle has a radius). Disposing the canvas finishes the file and writes it to the stream, which is left open. An image or picture drawn several times is stored once, as it was when first drawn.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgClip
files.Summary: A clip path, in the coordinates of the node it clips: the union of its shapes, each with its own clip-rule.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgComment
files.Summary: An XML comment, kept so a save writes it back.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgContent
files.Summary: One item of an 's content, in file order: an element, text, a comment or a processing instruction.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgContentList
files.Summary: An element's content in file order: child elements, text, comments and processing instructions. Changes mark the document's render tree for rebuilding.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgDecodeOptions
files.Summary: Options for reading SVG through with Raster.Load and Raster.Probe.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgDocument
files.Summary: An SVG document: an editable element tree read from an .svg or .svgz file, which saves back to SVG and draws through Egami.Drawing's canvas.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgElement
files.Summary: An element of an SVG document's editable tree: its name and namespace, attributes and content, like XDocument's elements. Unknown elements and foreign namespaces (Inkscape's, Illustrator's metadata) are kept, so a save writes them back.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgException
files.Summary: Thrown when an SVG file is not well-formed XML, breaks a safety limit, or, with , has anything a lenient load would skip.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgFilter
files.Summary: A filter, in the coordinates of the node it filters: the filter elements and CSS filter functions of its filter property, run one after the other.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgFontOptions
files.Summary: Where a document's text finds its fonts (question 13): the caller's first, then the fonts installed on the machine unless is off, then per-character fallback through the same fonts. A server that renders untrusted files should pass its own collection and turn system fonts off, so output never depends on the machine.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgFormat
files.Summary: SVG and SVGZ as an Egami format: registered with , Raster.Load draws an SVG file at its own size (times ) and Raster.Probe gives that size without drawing. The format only reads; nothing outside the file is opened, so images it links are not drawn, and text uses the machine's fonts. For a resolver, your own fonts, a target size or a background, load an and call .

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgGlyphRenderer
files.Summary: Draws the glyphs of an OpenType SVG table (question 20): each glyph's document is read once per font and kept, and the element glyphid is drawn in the font's units, its origin on the baseline. Set it on ; uses it already.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgGroup
files.Summary: A group of nodes drawn in order: a g, svg, a, switch, a use instance or a marker.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgImage
files.Summary: An image: a raster drawn into a rectangle, or another SVG document drawn as a group.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgImageFormat
files.Summary: The format embeds drawn images in.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgLoadOptions
files.Summary: How reads a file: what it may fetch, how strict it is, and which limits and diagnostics apply.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgMask
files.Summary: A mask, in the coordinates of the node it masks: content drawn into a region, used by luminance or alpha.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgNamespaces
files.Summary: The XML namespaces SVG files use.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgNode
files.Summary: A node of a document's render tree: the elements resolved for drawing, with styles applied, units in pixels, use expanded, references linked and shapes turned into paths, as resvg's usvg tree. It is immutable, so a document that is not being edited can be drawn on many threads at once.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgPaintOrder
files.Summary: Which of a shape's fill, stroke and markers is painted first (paint-order).

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgPath
files.Summary: A shape: a 2.6 with its fill, stroke and markers.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgProcessingInstruction
files.Summary: An XML processing instruction, such as <?xml-stylesheet ...?>, kept so a save writes it back.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgRenderOptions
files.Summary: How and draw a document.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgResolvers
files.Summary: Ready resolvers for .

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgSaveOptions
files.Summary: How writes a document.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgTextContent
files.Summary: Character data in an element: text or a CDATA section, kept apart so a save writes it back the same way.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgTextMode
files.Summary: How writes text.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgTextRun
files.Summary: Text: one run of positioned glyphs in one font with one fill and stroke, drawn with so a PDF or SVG canvas keeps real text. A text element becomes a group of these and of the paths of its decorations.

files.Title: Egami.Svg.SvgWriteOptions
files.Summary: How writes SVG: text, number precision, layout, image format and fallback resolution.

files.Title: Egami.UnsupportedFormatException
files.Summary: Thrown when no registered format matches the data, or the matching format cannot read or write.

files.Title: Egami.YuvConvertOptions
files.Summary: The chroma filters for conversions between a and a .

files.Title: Egami.YuvPlane<TSample>
files.Summary: One plane of a : a width × height grid of raw samples, stored row by row. A row is always one contiguous span. Samples are stored low-bit aligned: a 10-bit sample is 0 to 1023 in a .

files.Title: Egami.YuvRaster<TSample>
files.Summary: A picture held as separate Y, U, V and optional alpha planes of TSample samples. See .

files.Title: Egami.YuvRaster
files.Summary: A picture held as separate luma (Y) and chroma (U, V) planes, plus an optional alpha plane, the way video codecs, AVIF, lossy WebP and JPEG store it. This base class is used when the sample type is not known at compile time; gives the planes. Convert to and from a with , and .

files.Title: Egami.YuvRasterInfo
files.Summary: What reads from a header: the image as describes it, and the planes would give, if any.
